title: Unit lattice faces: parametrization, Hausdorff measure, integrals, diameter, closedness and separation (Simon Ch. 6, §5; step 1 of the parent proof)
statement: Conventions (as in the selected node): ℝ^P = Euclid P, ℝⁿ = Euclid n, Hᵈ = μHE[d], e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 ∈ ℝ^P, x_i the i-th coordinate. n := m + 1. For a pair p = (z, ι) ∈ ℤ^P × (Fin n → Fin P): Φ_p(y) := z + Σ_{j<n} y_j e_{ι(j)} for y ∈ ℝⁿ (Lean: WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.1 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.2 j) (1 : ℝ)); e_p := (e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(m)}); Q₁ := {y ∈ ℝⁿ : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i} with Lebesgue measure (volume); F_p := {x ∈ ℝ^P : z_i ≤ x_i ≤ z_i + 1 for i ∈ range ι, x_i = z_i for i ∉ range ι} (the closed unit face of the selected node's statement); A_p := Φ_p(Q₁) (the open face). 𝒟^d(U) = TestFormOn U d and 𝒟_d(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U d (domain univ throughout); ∂X = X.boundary; M_W(X) = X.massOn W and M(X) = X.mass (Euclidean coefficient norm covectorEuclideanNorm); IMRep and IsIntegerMultiplicity are the contract notions. Statement: let P, m ∈ ℕ and p = (z, ι) with ι strictly increasing. Then (1) volume(Q₁) = 1; (2) Hⁿ(F_p) = 1 (Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^P); (3) Hⁿ⌞F_p = Φ_p#(volume⌞Q₁), i.e. μHE[n].restrict F_p = Measure.map Φ_p (volume.restrict Q₁); (4) ∫_{F_p} f dHⁿ = ∫_{Q₁} f(Φ_p(y)) dy for every function f : ℝ^P → ℝ; (5) Φ_p(y) ∈ F_p whenever 0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1 for all i; (6) dist(Φ_p(y), Φ_p(y')) = dist(y, y') for all y, y' ∈ ℝⁿ; (7) dist(x, x') ≤ √P for all x, x' ∈ F_p; (8) F_p is closed; (9) for every pair q = (z', ι') with ι' strictly increasing and q ≠ p, and every y ∈ Q₁, Φ_p(y) ∉ F_q.
